In one night shift in small surgical ward I was covering eight patients with one other nurse. During medication round I have seen new enoxaparin order for a patient which creatinine was doubled in that morning. I held the dose because drug is clearing through the kidneys and bleeding risk is rising when function falls, I called the on-call physician, I read back labs and I got renal adjusted dose. Patient did not have bleeding, and the ward has adopted my proposal for a pharmacy alert about renal function inside one month. In rural clinic without doctor on site, this habit to check labs before to give a dose is what is keeping patients safe.
